Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

## Diagnosis

The current bug report describes that the precision of the method `c0.m0()` is limited by machine epsilon. It mentions that when using this method with many treatments, p-values are continuous down to 2.2e-16 but drop to 0 after that. This behavior is similar to an issue described in [MATH-201](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/MATH-201) related to T-test p-value precision being hampered by machine epsilon.

Looking at the failing test `org.apache.commons.math.stat.correlation.SpearmansRankCorrelationTest.testPValueNearZero()`, it creates a dataset with high dimensions where the p-values diminish smoothly but vanish at a certain dimension, resulting in p-values close to 1E-303. This could be an indication of precision limitations similar to the issue reported.

### Fault Localization
Inspecting the code snippet of method `c0.m0()` would provide further insights into how the p-values are calculated and why they might be dropping to 0 after a certain point.
